title: Dévissage des complexes ½ simpliciaux ∂ - parfaits et structures multiplicatives… (1975 ou 1976) : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting: k is a ring (later noetherian). L. is a half-simplicial (semi-simplicial: face maps only) k-module. The previous page introduced 'very special' (très spécial) L.: those isomorphic to a direct sum of standard pieces.
- Acyclic pieces Λ^iE ⊗ M_i (i ≥ 1), with rank in degree n equal to μ_i·C(n+1,i). Here E is the standard semi-simplicial module with E_n = Z^{n+1}.
- Homological pieces N_j, with rank in degree n equal to ν_j·C(n,j) = ν_j·P_j(n), where ν_j = rk H_j(L.).
Thus f_L(n) = rk L_n = Σ_{i≥1} μ_i C(n+1,i) + Σ_j ν_j C(n,j). The previous page showed that the C(n+1,i) form a Z-basis of integer-valued polynomials, so f_L and the ν_j determine the μ_i, hence L. up to isomorphism.

This page solves the inverse (realisation) problem. Given integers ν_j ≥ 0 (finitely many nonzero) and an integer-valued polynomial f, when is there a very special L. with rk H_j = ν_j and f_L(n) = f(n) for large n?
- Put g = f − Σ ν_j P_j. This is again an integer-valued polynomial, so g = Σ_{i≥0} μ_i C(n+1,i) with (μ_i) ∈ Z^(N) unique.
- Answer: such L. exists iff μ_0 = 0 and μ_i ≥ 0 for i ≥ 1. Sufficiency: take free modules of ranks μ_i, ν_j and form the corresponding direct sum.
- Since C(0,i) = 0 for i ≥ 1, we get μ_0 = g(−1) = f(−1) − Σ ν_j C(−1,j) = f(−1) − Σ (−1)^j ν_j.
- Hence μ_0 = 0 ⇔ f(−1) = Σ (−1)^j ν_j = χ(L.). In words: the rank polynomial evaluated at −1 is the Euler characteristic of the homology.

The page ends with an aborted draft of the definition of '(strictly) ∂-perfect' semi-simplicial modules: L.^! (the Dold–Puppe chain complex) is a (strictly) perfect complex. This is formalised as Déf 1 / Prop 1 on the next page. The purpose is a dévissage/classification of strictly ∂-perfect semi-simplicial modules by rank data, preparing a structure theorem (Prop 1c: successive extensions of Λ^iE ⊗ M_i) and later multiplicative structures.
errors: No mathematical error. The identity (−1)(−2)…(−j)/j! = (−1)^j = C(−1,j) is correct, and so is the equivalence μ_0 = 0 ⇔ f(−1) = χ.

Minor implicit assumptions: f is integer-valued; only finitely many ν_j are nonzero (needed for g to be polynomial and for χ to make sense); 'très spécial' excludes the i = 0 piece Λ^0E, which is why μ_0 = 0 is required.

ideas.what: Classification of 'very special' semi-simplicial modules by the rank polynomial plus homology ranks, using the binomial basis C(n+1,i) of integer-valued polynomials
ideas.modern_name: Dold–Kan-type rank decomposition; Pólya/binomial basis of integer-valued polynomials

ideas.what: Rank polynomial evaluated at −1 equals the Euler characteristic, f_L(−1) = χ(L.)
ideas.modern_name: Euler characteristic as value at −1 of the simplex-count polynomial (combinatorial-reciprocity flavour)
ideas.usually_credited_to: folklore (simplicial sets with finitely many nondegenerate simplices: #X_n = Σ a_k C(n,k), evaluated at n = −1 gives χ)

ideas.what: Notion of (strictly) ∂-perfect / ∂-pseudo-coherent semi-simplicial module via the Dold–Puppe complex
ideas.modern_name: perfect complexes transported to semi-simplicial modules
ideas.usually_credited_to: perfect complexes: Grothendieck/Illusie SGA 6; the semi-simplicial variant unclear
ideas.where_published: SGA 6 for perfect and pseudo-coherent complexes; the ∂-variants are probably unpublished

missed.claim: The page begins, and the next pages continue, a classification theory of strictly ∂-perfect semi-simplicial modules by numerical invariants (rank polynomial plus homology ranks), with χ = f(−1). It is aimed at dévissage and multiplicative (λ-ring-like) structures. As far as I know this programme was never written up. The realisation criterion itself is elementary.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is only a minor footnote. It anticipates a K-theory/Euler-characteristic bookkeeping for semi-simplicial (Δ_inj) modules, which are again of interest (semi-simplicial models, ∞-categories without degeneracies). Little new mathematical content.

deep.surprise_reason: An elementary combinatorial computation (binomial bases, the Euler characteristic as f(−1)) inside a routine development. It is correct and neat but standard; only its context (the unpublished ∂-perfect programme) is of historical interest.
transcription_corrections: 'dim.-parfait' / 'strictly dim.-parfait' should read '∂-parfait' / 'strictly ∂-parfait', matching the terminology of the next page.

Bottom definition reads roughly: 'Modules ½ simpliciaux L. str. "∂-parfait" = tels que L.^! soit un complexe de chaînes de k-modules parfait (str. parfait)'. 'un complexe de dim[?]' should be 'un complexe de chaînes'.

Line 1: the crossed-out text is 'rg π_j(L.)'; the intended reading is 'Si on se donne des ν_j ≥ 0 entiers (j ≥ 0) et une fonction polynomiale f(n) à valeurs entières pour les entiers n, à quelle condition existe-t-il L. très spécial…'.
'(−1)(−2)…(−j)/j!' is correctly read; the dots are implicit in the manuscript.
'donc on a ainsi[?]' may be 'donc on a en fait'; uncertain.
